title: Compiler diagnostics are structured only at the external CLI boundary
observed_need: Compile-fail and diagnostic tests must match diagnostic identity and preserve source spans without scraping human prose.
current_language_behavior: The Rust toolchain exposes versioned structured diagnostics and the native runner fail-closes on invalid admission. P-062 added a Test-owned MNCS application that projects diagnostic codes and applies compile verdict policy without building a host diagnostic-code list. P-063 replaces the verdict application's Test JsonValue tree projection with bounded Stdlib JSON cursor events and a syntax validator. P-064 added bounded native typed records for standard diagnostic objects; P-065 extended them with expected tokens and one level of related diagnostics. P-066 replaced the diagnostic projector's JsonValue tree traversal with a second bounded json_cursor pass over the original chunked bytes. P-067 retires the fixed native diagnostic-record output array and Python reconstruction mapper: MNCS validates the selected array and returns its source span, then Python decodes only that span for the public dictionary contract. P-068 removes the redundant per-field typed validation buffers; the native cursor now validates JSON and selection metadata, bounds the selected array, and preserves arbitrary diagnostic JSON values in the selected span. P-069 feeds that selected span through the existing Test-owned MNCS JSON token tape; Python validates token coordinates against the source and assembles the public list and dictionaries from native structural events, while decoding only scalar tokens. MNCS application code still cannot directly consume compiler Diagnostic values.
why_insufficient: Python still materializes public dictionaries and lists and decodes individual JSON scalar tokens. The native token stream is limited to 512 tokens; invalid documents, unsupported root shapes, excessive nesting, arrays beyond 32 entries or 32 object diagnostics, token-bound declines, execution-budget exhaustion, and oversized documents retain the Python compatibility parser. All paths still cross the structured CLI JSON boundary.
minimal_reproducer: tests/fixtures/compile_fail.mncs plus tools/mncs_test.py: compile_entry sends the compiler document to the native diagnostic span selector, then passes the selected array bytes through the Test-owned MNCS token tape before Python materializes the public diagnostic values.
desired_direction: A versioned diagnostic value/protocol exposing code, severity, source span, related diagnostics, and rendered forms to native tooling.
workaround: The Test-owned native application validates up to 16,384 bytes with the Stdlib JSON cursor and syntax scanner, applies compile verdict policy, and returns the byte span for the selected root, errors, or diagnostics array when it has at most 32 items. A second native token pass validates up to 65,536 selected bytes and 512 tokens. Python checks token spans and assembles the public containers from native structure, decoding only scalar tokens. Invalid or over-bound documents retain the Python compatibility parser; no formatted-stderr parsing is used.
